extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists, mathematicians, and software users using primdec.lib, primdecint.lib, realrad.lib, reesclos.lib, sagbi.lib, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR libraries (primary decomposition, radicals, integral closure, real radical, primitive element computations, SAGBI-related routines). Each entry records usage, return value, notes, and examples for programmatic use.

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecSYE
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primdecSYE(I, c); I ideal, c int (optional). Return: a list pr of primary ideals and their associated primes: pr[i][1] the i-th primary component, pr[i][2] the i-th prime component. If I is the unit ideal returns an empty list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm of Shimoyama/Yokoyama. Options: c=0 use given variable ordering; c=1 (default) minAssChar tries to use an optimal ordering; c=2 use minAssGTZ; c=3 use minAssGTZ and facstd. For local orderings result considered in localization of polynomial ring (not power series). For local and mixed orderings, specifying string 'global' as third argument returns decomposition in corresponding global ring. Examples provided showing LIB "primdec.lib" usage and sample outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssGTZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minAssGTZ(I[, l]); I ideal, l list (optional). Return: a list, the minimal associated prime ideals of proper ideal I, otherwise ideal(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters in list l: 0, "facstd" -> uses facstd first (default); 1, "noFacstd" -> does not use facstd; "GTZ" -> original Gianni/Trager/Zacharias algorithm; "SL" -> GTZ with Laplagne modifications (default). Designed for characteristic 0, also works in char k>0 via Yokoyama algorithm. For local orderings, result is in localization of polynomial ring; for local and mixed, specify 'global' as second argument to return decomposition in global ring. Example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssGTZE
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minAssGTZE(I[, l]); I ideal, l list (optional). Return: a list, the minimal associated prime ideals of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same optional parameters as minAssGTZ (facstd/noFacstd, GTZ/SL). Designed for characteristic 0, works also in char k>0 via Yokoyama. For local orderings, result considered in localization; for local/mixed, specify 'global' as second argument. Example and sample outputs shown; returns empty list for unit ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssChar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minAssChar(I[,c]); I ideal, c int (optional). Return: list, the minimal associated prime ideals of I. If I is the unit ideal returns list( ideal(1) ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If c=0 uses given ordering; otherwise system tries to find an optimal ordering to speed algorithm. For local orderings, result in localization of polynomial ring. For local/mixed orderings, specifying string 'global' as third argument returns decomposition in corresponding global ring. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssCharE
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minAssCharE(I[,c]); I ideal, c int (optional). Return: list, the minimal associated prime ideals of I. If I is the unit ideal returns an empty list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same ordering/optimization behavior as minAssChar: c=0 uses given ordering; otherwise tries optimal ordering. Local/mixed ordering notes identical: localization vs power series ring and 'global' option to return global decomposition. Examples and sample outputs shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: testPrimary
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testPrimary(pr,k); pr a list, k an ideal. Assume pr is the result of primdecGTZ(k) or primdecSY(k). Return: int, 1 if the intersection of the ideals in pr is k, 0 if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to validate that a purported primary decomposition recomposes to the original ideal. Example demonstrates usage with primdecGTZ and testPrimary returning 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: testPrimaryE
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testPrimaryE(pr,k); pr a list, k an ideal. Assume pr is the result of a primary decomposition and may be empty (for the unit ideal). Return: int, 1 if the intersection of the ideals in pr is k, 0 if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variant of testPrimary that accepts empty decomposition (unit ideal). Example demonstrates usage and return value 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: radical
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: radical(I[, l]); I ideal, l list (optional). Return: ideal, the radical of I (or the equiradical if required in input parameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters: 0,"fullRad" -> full radical (default); 1,"equiRad" -> equiradical; "KL" -> Krick/Logar algorithm; "SL" -> Laplagne modifications (default); "facstd" -> uses facstd first (default for non-homogeneous ideals); "noFacstd" -> does not use facstd (default for homogeneous ideals). Implemented using a combination of Krick/Logar (Laplagne mods) and Kemper's algorithms; works in positive characteristic (Kemper's algorithm). Example shows usage and output.

rubrics_metrics.name: radicalEHV
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: radicalEHV(i); i ideal. Return: ideal, the radical of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses algorithm of Eisenbud/Huneke/Vasconcelos which reduces computation to complete intersection case by taking generic linear combinations. Works only in characteristic 0 or large p. Example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: equiRadical
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: equiRadical(I); I ideal. Return: ideal, intersection of associated primes of I of maximal dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements combination of Krick/Logar (with Laplagne mods) and Kemper; works in positive characteristic. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: prepareAss
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: prepareAss(I); I ideal. Return: list, the radicals of the maximal dimensional components of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses algorithm of Eisenbud/Huneke/Vasconcelos. Example provided showing returned radicals for sample ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: equidim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: equidim(I) or equidim(I,1); I ideal. Return: list of equidimensional ideals a[1],...,a[s] with: a[s] the equidimensional locus of I (intersection of primary ideals of dimension of I), a[1]..a[s-1] the lower dimensional equidimensional loci. If I is the unit ideal returns a list containing the unit ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An embedded component q (primary ideal) of I can be replaced in the decomposition by a primary ideal q1 with same radical. equidim(I,1) uses algorithm of Eisenbud/Huneke/Vasconcelos. Example output included.

rubrics_metrics.name: equidimMax
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: equidimMax(i); i ideal. Return: ideal of equidimensional locus (of maximal dimension) of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows equidimMax(i) returning the maximal equidimensional component (e.g., _[1]=z).

rubrics_metrics.name: equidimMaxEHV
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: equidimMaxEHV(I); I ideal. Return: ideal, the equidimensional component (of maximal dimension) of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses algorithm of Eisenbud, Huneke and Vasconcelos. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: zerodec
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: zerodec(I); I ideal. Assume: I is zero-dimensional, ground field characteristic 0. Return: list of primary ideals, the zero-dimensional decomposition of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm (of Monico) works well only for small total number of solutions (vdim(std(I)) < 100) and without parameters. In practice works in large char p>0 but may fail for small p. If printlevel>0 additional information displayed. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: absPrimdecGTZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: absPrimdecGTZ(I); I ideal. Assume: ground field has characteristic 0. Return: a ring containing two lists: absolute_primes (absolute prime components of I) and primary_decomp (output of primdecGTZ(I)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry absolute_primes[i] describes a class of conjugated absolute primes: absolute_primes[i][1] the absolute prime component, absolute_primes[i][2] the number of conjugates. The first entry of absolute_primes[i][1] is the minimal polynomial of a minimal finite field extension needed. For local and mixed orderings, localization/global remarks as elsewhere. Note: Algorithm of Gianni/Trager/Zacharias combined with absFactorize. Example demonstrates creation of new ring S and how to setring S; absolute_primes to access results. See also absFactorize and primdecGTZ references.

rubrics_metrics.name: absPrimdecGTZE
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: absPrimdecGTZE(I); I ideal. Assume: ground field has characteristic 0. Return: a ring containing two lists: absolute_primes and primary_decomp. Will fail for unit ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same interpretation of absolute_primes as absPrimdecGTZ. For local/mixed orderings, specify 'global' as second argument to get global decomposition. Algorithm of Gianni/Trager/Zacharias combined with absFactorize. Example provided and cross-references to absFactorize and primdecGTZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: sep
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sep(f[,1]); Example shown: ring R=(5,t,s),(x,y,z),dp; poly f=(x^25-t*x^5+t)*(x^3+s); sep(f,1); Return: printed output showing components and a polynomial (example shows printed polynomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No full API prose in this chunk; example demonstrates calling sep on a polynomial with parameters and getting outputs. Useful for separation computations (context implied by name and example).

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primdecZ(I[, n]); I ideal, n integer (number of processors). Return: a list pr of primary ideals and their associated primes: pr[i][1] the i-th primary component, pr[i][2] the i-th prime component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library primdecint.lib: primary decomposition in polynomial rings over integers Z[x1,...,xn]. primdecZ can be used in parallel. Note about size(#) indicating available processors. Reference: Pﬁster, Sadiq, Steidel 'An Algorithm for primary decomposition in polynomial rings over the integers' (arXiv:1008.2074). Examples show usage and sample outputs including handling various integer ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecZM
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primdecZM(N); N module. Return: a list pr of primary modules and their associated primes: pr[i][1] the i-th primary component, pr[i][2] the i-th prime component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided showing module decomposition outputs. Part of primdecint.lib for modules over integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minAssZ(I); I ideal. Return: a list pr of associated primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows usage on integer ideals; returns associated prime data (e.g., pairs of integers/primes and variables). Part of primdecint.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: radicalZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: radicalZ(I); I ideal. Return: the radical of the input ideal (over integers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates radicalZ returning combined integer/variable expressions. Part of primdecint.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: heightZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: heightZ(I); I ideal. Return: the height of the input ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows heightZ(I) returning integer height (e.g., 1). Part of primdecint.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: equidimZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: equidimZ(I); I ideal. Return: the part of minimal height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows equidimZ(I) returning elements (e.g., _[1]=3). Part of primdecint.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectZ
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: intersectZ(...). Return: the intersection of the input ideals (over integers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: alternative to intersect(I,J) over integers; faster for some examples and useful for debugging. Extensive example shows progressive intersection of many integer ideals and the resulting generators (I[1]=..., I[2]=...). Part of primdecint.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: primitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primitive(i); i ideal. Assume: i is given by generators m[1],...,m[n] such that for j=1,...,n: m[j] is a polynomial in k[x(1),...,x(j)] and m[j](a[1],...,a[j-1],x(j)) is the minimal polynomial for a[j] over k(a[1],...,a[j-1]). Return: ideal j in k[x(n)] with j[1] a minimal polynomial for a primitive element b of k(a[1],...,a[n]) over k, and j[2]..j[n+1] polynomials in k[x(n)] such that j[i+1](b)=a[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of variables in basering must equal n (number of given generators). If ground field k has few elements it may happen no linear combination is primitive; primitive(i) returns zero ideal then and one should use primitive_extra(i). Examples show use over Q and sample outputs (minpoly and expressions mapping back).

rubrics_metrics.name: primitive_extra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primitive_extra(i); i ideal. Assume: ground field k = Q or Z/pZ and ideal i is given by 2 generators f,g where f is minimal polynomial of a in k[x] and g in k[x,y] with g(a,y) minimal polynomial of b in k(a)[y]. Return: ideal j in k[y] such that j[1] is minimal polynomial for primitive element c of k(a,b) over k and j[2] is polynomial with j[2](c)=a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: primitive_extra tries all elements of k(a,b) and therefore always finds a primitive element (so is reliable when primitive() may fail in finite fields). Field extensions like Z/pZ(a) are not allowed as ground field for this routine. primitive_extra assumes second generator g is monic in (k[x])[y]. Example given using ring over 3 and showing returned minimal polynomial and primitive element expression. Note: intended for small-degree/2-generator cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: splitring
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: splitring(f[,L]); f poly (univariate and irreducible over active ring), L list of polys and/or ideals (optional). Return: a new ring (an algebraic extension) where f splits (or where primitive root of f is adjoined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active ring must allow algebraic extension (not a transcendental extension of Q or Z/p). If second parameter L provided, output ring defines list erg = L mapped to new ring; if basering minpoly non-zero then primitive root image appended to erg. If old ring has no parameter, name a used for parameter (or next free name), otherwise keep parameter name and change minimal polynomial. Names of ring variables and orderings unaffected. Examples show changing to Q(sqrt(2)) and further nested extensions, and the returned basering/minpoly information.

rubrics_metrics.name: realpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: realpoly(f); f a univariate polynomial. Return: poly f, where f is the real part of the input f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior on various rings: realpoly returns the 'real part' polynomial (illustrative examples include multivariate polynomials, products with (x^2+y^2+1) etc.). Part of realrad.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: realzero
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: realzero(j); j a zero-dimensional ideal. Return: j: a zero dimensional ideal, which is the real radical of i if dim(i)=0; 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internals: acts via primary decomposition (i=1), listdecomp (i=2) or facstd (i=3). Examples include non-parametric fields and parametric examples with ring having parameter t to show returned ideals for each path. Part of realrad.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: realrad
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: realrad(id), id an ideal of arbitrary dimension. Return: the real radical of id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates use on mixture of zero-dimensional and dimension-1 ideals and returns a list of polynomials representing the real radical. Part of realrad.lib; example outputs are long polynomials illustrating complexity of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReesAlgebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ReesAlgebra(I); I = ideal. Return: a list containing two rings: [1] a ring RR in which an ideal ker is defined such that R[It] = RR/ker; [2] a ring Kxt the basering with additional variable t containing an ideal mapI that defines map RR -> Kxt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute the Rees algebra R[It] as an affine ring for I in R=k[x1..xn]. Example shows returned Rees ring, variable names (x y U(1) U(2) U(3)), and kernel generators (ker[1]..ker[6]). Useful precursor for computing integral closures via Rees algebra. Part of reesclos.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalI
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: normalI(I [,p [,r [,l]]]); I an ideal, p, r, l optional integers. Return: list containing I^p and the integral closure(s) of powers of I (depending on parameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: normalI computes the integral closure of I in polynomial ring R using Rees algebra and normal.lib. If p not given or p==0, computes closure of all powers up to max degree in t occurring in closure of R[It]. If r==1 then I^p whose closure is not just sum/product of smaller. normalI starts by checking whether I is radical. If l==1 then uses locNormal instead of normal to compute normalization. Displays more comments for higher printlevel. Returns list of closures as ideals of basering. Example shows normalI on sample ideal returning added generator (xy3).

rubrics_metrics.name: sagbiSPoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sagbiSPoly(A[, returnRing, meth]); A is an ideal, returnRing and meth are integers. Return: ideal or ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: returns SAGBI S-polynomials of the leading terms of given ideal A if returnRing=0; otherwise returns a new ring containing ideals algebraicRelations and spolynomials. meth determines method for computing algebraic relations: meth=0 (default) uses std, meth=1 uses slimgb, meth=2 uses toric ideal. Assumes basering is not a qring. Example demonstrates computing S-polynomials, returning extended ring, accessing 'spolynomials' and 'algebraicRelations', and verifying substitution. Part of sagbi.lib.
